full_judgment: 57. Mr. Hamidul Huq Chowdhury has made serious efforts to show that the sale-deed is not genuine but is the result of fraud, inducement and misrepresentation. He has contended that in one sale-deed 20 persons who had no community of interests joined as vendors for the sale of different plots of land and that such a collective sale is an unusual matter. We do not think that they had no community of interest at all, for they were members of the minority community living, and having landed properties, in the same village and decided to migrate to India in a hurry on account of the communal disturbances from which they just escaped. They decided to sell their lands together in order to expedite their migration. Execution of a common document by several vendors is not irregular if the lands sought to be transferred have been specifically described in the sale-deed. Mr. Chowdhury next contends that no reliance can be placed upon the Agreement, Ext-A as it was not mentioned in the sale-deed. Ext B. The Agreement, Mr. Chowdhury further contends, is a subsequent creation. D.W. 1. Hammad, the recipient of the kabala has explained that the Agreement was not mentioned in the sale-deed due to inadvertence. But when Manindra, son-in-law of the plaintiff, was the scribe of the Agreement why lie was not produced by the plaintiff to say that it was not written by him on 28-12-64 or that it was not written by him at all. The scribe going to be the plaintiff's son-in-law can hardly be relied upon as a witness by the defendant when his father-in-law disowned the whole transaction. Mr. Chovvdhury's next contention is that low consideration of the sale-deed raises a presumption of fraud or undue influence. Consideration of the sale-deed does not appear to be low, for 2.66 (two acres, sixty decimals of land was sold at Tk. 14,900/-as shown in the sale deed, but the plaintiffs put a much bigger area-16 acres, in their plaint, a claim which got no basis at all.
